title: Combinatorial sufficient conditions for graph rigidity and applications to random graphs
summary: A graph $G=(V,E)$ is called $d$-rigid if, for a generic embedding of its vertices in $\mathbb{R}^d$, every edge-length preserving continuous motion of the vertices preserves the distances between all pairs of non-adjacent vertices as well. In this paper, we present several new results on the rigidity of random graphs. In particular, we show that there exists $c>0$ such that, for $p\ge 2 \log{n}/n$, the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ is with high probability (whp) $\lfloor c n p\rfloor$-rigid.
